How it works. Each picture is cut to a centred square of 100 × 100 pixels: one 4-level symbol per pixel in black & white, three in colour (64 colours). Every wrong pixel is a real decision our receiver made on the lab bench: PolSK-4 and ASK-4 were recorded through the identical emulated turbulence at 10 MBd, and each Transmit replays one matched pair of recordings at the chosen strength from a random starting point. Pixels arrive in the order they are sent; yellow marks an error as it lands. Scan the QR code to send your own photo from your phone: it goes straight to this screen and is never stored.
Why polarisation wins. A turbulent fade dims the whole beam. Brightness levels (ASK) get confused, but the ratio between the two polarisations (PolSK) barely changes.
